_metadata.description: Sample geometry theorem records for development and testing.

_metadata.curriculum_context: Sri Lankan GCE O/L Mathematics — Geometry (Circle Theorems and Cyclic Quadrilaterals)

theorems.name: Opposite Angles of a Cyclic Quadrilateral
theorems.statement: The opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary; that is, they sum to 180 degrees.
theorems.conditions: The quadrilateral must be inscribed in a circle (all four vertices lie on the circle).

theorems.name: Angles in the Same Segment
theorems.statement: Angles subtended by the same arc at the circumference of a circle are equal.
theorems.conditions: Both angles must be inscribed angles subtending the same arc and lying on the same side of the chord.

theorems.name: Angle in a Semicircle
theorems.statement: The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is 90 degrees.
theorems.conditions: The angle must be inscribed in the semicircle (the vertex lies on the circle and the subtending chord is a diameter).

theorems.name: Exterior Angle of a Cyclic Quadrilateral
theorems.statement: The exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior opposite angle.
theorems.conditions: The exterior angle is formed by extending one side of the quadrilateral; the quadrilateral must be cyclic.

theorems.name: Tangent–Radius Perpendicularity
theorems.statement: A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency.
theorems.conditions: The line must be tangent to the circle (touches at exactly one point).

theorems.name: Alternate Segment Theorem (Tangent–Chord Angle)
theorems.statement: The angle between a tangent to a circle and a chord drawn from the point of tangency equals the inscribed angle subtending the same arc on the opposite side.
theorems.conditions: A tangent and a chord must meet at the point of tangency on the circle.
